prerequisites: Basic knowledge of manufacturing processes and their selection based on product and components
Notions of design and its relationship with involved manufacturing processes
Continuous handling of aspects related to molding and machining processes, as well as their automatic control.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context
Students know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study

Students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous manner.

Prepare technical specifications that allow posing a problem in mechatronic engineering maintaining a global and integrative vision and using prescriptive, procedural or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.

Acquire the necessary skills to act as administrators of mechatronic systems design, assuming planning (setting goals and strategies), organization (assigning tasks and resources, coordinating), direction (leading and motivating) and control (monitoring) functions.

Evaluate the viability of new mechatronic products, based on their technological characteristics, manufacturing possibilities and other socio-economic factors related to their possible implementation.
Document the specification, implementation and commissioning of mechatronic equipment and systems taking into account technical aspects and relevant regulatory standards.
Develop skills for working in cooperative and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Carry out the technical direction of teams of specialist engineers in multidisciplinary projects and maintenance of industrial equipment and facilities.
Plan the manufacturing processes of the components of a mechatronic system taking into account the restrictions imposed by the manufacturing, assembly and verification environment.
Plan the assembly, commissioning and maintenance of mechatronic equipment or system.
Identify the subcomponents of a technologically complex system, the interactions between them, and the effects and consequences of their possible redesign.
Acquire knowledge, techniques and skills that increase research and innovation potential and promote technology transfer to industry.
Know and be able to practically apply the technical requirements and specifications necessary for generating the manufacturing documentation required for prototype development.
Understand the basic aspects of processes that can be applied in the manufacturing of prototypes or short runs.
Be able to adequately select the most suitable processes for the manufacturing of prototypes or short runs.
Be able to plan and select the most suitable working conditions in prototyping processes by molding and material removal.
Understand the physical fundamentals and workflow in additive manufacturing processes.
Be able to practically apply knowledge of prototyping and additive manufacturing to the creation of functional models of parts.
Be able to carry out basic reverse engineering tasks.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, involvement accounts for 20% and assignments/projects account for 80% of the grade. Projects are graded from 0 to 10, where 0 is for non-submission. For extraordinary examinations, students must take a theoretical-practical test representing 100% of the global qualification. Differentiated evaluation, if approved, also consists of a theoretical-practical test representing 100% of the global qualification. Grades will be published via Campus Virtual, and students have 24 hours to request a review via email after publication.
